Which festival and date the Pashupatinath gate video shows

properties.statement: Fact-checkers give different accounts of when and during which festival the Pashupatinath Temple gate video was recorded: Naxal Bhagwati Jatra on 31 March 2025, Basleshwori Jatra at the end of March 2025, or the Vatsaleshwori Jatra about two months before 9 September.
properties.verification_note: Newschecker gives 31 March 2025 and the Naxal Bhagwati Jatra. BOOM gives the second day of the Basleshwori Jatra, around the end of March 2025. Alt News and AFP also say Naxal Bhagwati Jatra. IPS, summarising a fact-check, says the clip was uploaded nearly two months earlier during the Vatsaleshwori Jatra. The three festival names and the two dates are not reconciled in the sources. All agree it was an older festival video and not a protest.

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: Indian TV claim that rioters tried to vandalise Pashupatinath Temple before the army deployed

properties.statement: A Zee News anchor said that rioters hiding within the crowd of protesters attempted to vandalise Pashupatinath Temple and that the army was deployed only after this incident. Other Indian outlets aired the same footage as an attack on the temple.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. A temple monk told AFP that everything was peaceful inside the temple. The footage was an older ritual, see claim:video-shows-protesters-storming-pashupatinath-temple.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: Indonesian video shown as Nepali protesters attacking police

properties.statement: A video of police sheltering behind riot shields under attack was shared on 10 September 2025 as showing Nepali protesters attacking police.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Alt News traced the video to protests in Indonesia in late August 2025; The Quint's weekly recap reports the same finding. Alt News says the national editor of the Hindi daily Dainik Bhaskar was among those who shared it.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: Video of a slingshot attack on 'Malacañang Palace' shows Nepal's Parliament

properties.statement: A video showing a masked protester shooting at Malacañang Palace in the Philippines with a slingshot was widely shared.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. VERA Files says the footage was taken in front of Nepal's Parliament Building. The original Facebook post, with more than 10 million views, had been taken down by the time of the fact-check. Single fact-checker.

entities.title: Nepal protest video shared as anti-Modi protests in India

properties.statement: Videos of protests in Nepal were shared with captions saying that India was in turmoil and that Narendra Modi's government faced protests.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Rumor Scanner located one video in Nepalgunj (B.P. Chowk) during the 9 September 2025 protests and ran a second check on a similar caption. Both checks are by the same publisher.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: Sikkim rally video shown as Nepali protesters chanting for a Hindu nation or Modi

properties.statement: A video of a rally with 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' slogans was shared as Nepali protesters demanding a Hindu nation, calling for India's Hindu nation or marching in support of Narendra Modi.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. BOOM, Alt News and Digiteye each place the video in Sikkim. Their accounts of which Sikkim event it shows differ, see claim:sikkim-video-origin-event-conflict.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: Which Sikkim event the 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' video shows

properties.statement: Fact-checkers agree the video is from Sikkim but name different events: a rally attended by Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang on the eve of Independence Day, an Independence Day rally in Gangtok on 15 August 2025, or the 50th statehood anniversary celebrations on 29 May 2025.
properties.verification_note: BOOM: rally attended by the Sikkim chief minister on the eve of Independence Day. Alt News: Independence Day rally in Gangtok, 15 August 2025. Digiteye: 29 May 2025, Sikkim's 50th statehood anniversary, with a PIB report as support. The sources do not resolve the difference.

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: 2022 Pakistan video of tear gas canister being thrown back shown as Nepal

properties.statement: A video of a young man catching a tear gas canister and throwing it back was shared on 22 September 2025 as viral in Nepal.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Alt News traced it to a Gulf Today Facebook video uploaded on 25 May 2022 from Pakistan.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: Nepal Gen Z footage shared as a student protest in Chhattisgarh

properties.statement: In June 2026 a video of police using water cannon was shared on Instagram as students protesting over government job vacancies in Chhattisgarh, India.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: misleading. Fact Crescendo found the video originated from the September 2025 Gen Z protests in Nepal. Later reuse of the footage, outside the protest period.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: Photo of Yogi Adityanath poster shown as from the Gen Z protests

properties.statement: A photo of a poster of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was shared with the caption 'GenZ in Nepal wants something we already have', implying protesters carried it in September 2025.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. BOOM found the photo dates to 9 March 2025, at a pro-monarchy rally by the Rastriya Prajatantra Party welcoming former King Gyanendra Shah at Tribhuvan International Airport.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: Video of a man dragged into a river said to show Finance Minister Bishnu Paudel

properties.statement: A video of a man allegedly beaten and dragged into a river by protesters was shared by media outlets and on social media as showing Finance Minister Bishnu Paudel.
properties.verification_note: Media Diversity Institute reports that a fact-check found the man was not the finance minister; the underlying fact-check was not retrieved. Newslaundry (9 September) separately states that Deputy PM and Finance Minister Bishnu Paudel was beaten up by protesters, so the identity of this one video is contested, not the attack on the minister.

entities.title: Claim that 32 protesters or children were detained, disappeared or killed inside Parliament

properties.statement: Claims circulated that 32 Gen Z protesters, described in one version as children, had been detained or had disappeared inside the Parliament building and that their bodies were later found.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. The Diplomat Nepal calls the claim false; IPS describes a version in which police detained 32 children inside Parliament and the children were killed there, and calls it false. Neither source names a recovered body count matching the claim.

entities.title: Claim that Oli was the first and only Nepali PM never to visit India in office

properties.statement: On 9 September 2025 a journalist at WION and other social media users said KP Sharma Oli was the first and only Nepali prime minister who never visited India during his term.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Alt News and The Quint say Oli visited India as prime minister in 2016 and 2018. Alt News adds that the journalist later clarified in a thread that Oli had not visited during his third term.

properties.statement: A TikTok video was shared as a fresh interview of KP Sharma Oli after his resignation and the appointment of Sushila Karki as interim prime minister.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: misleading. Newschecker Nepal matched the clip to an interview posted on 30 July 2016, after Oli's first resignation as prime minister.

properties.statement: A TikTok video claimed that an international court had convicted former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli of crimes against humanity and sentenced him to death.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal says the video used a photo of a retired U.S. municipal judge who is well known online. Published 13 December 2025.

entities.title: Claim that Oli had been arrested (October 2025)

properties.statement: TikTok posts from 23 October 2025 suggested that former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli had been arrested.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal found no authority had ordered his arrest. The posts reused video of Prime Minister Karki leaving Shital Niwas after her oath on 12 September 2025.

properties.statement: A TikTok video posted on 2 October 2024 said Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli had suffered a heart attack and been taken to Grande Hospital.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: misleading. Newschecker Nepal says the footage was from a November 2018 hospital visit combined with false text. Build-up period, before the 2025 protests.

entities.title: Claim that Oli died after an accident (October 2024)

properties.statement: A TikTok post in October 2024 claimed Prime Minister Oli had been in an accident and died during treatment.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal found a press report (dated 4 Kartik 2081, about 20 October 2024) of Oli attending a CPN-UML secretariat meeting, and quoted his press coordinator as saying he was safe.

entities.title: Condolence posts claiming Oli had died (January 2025)

properties.statement: TikTok posts on 27 and 28 January 2025 offered condolences for Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli, claiming he had died.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal says Oli had only common cold symptoms and carried out official functions in person and virtually.

entities.title: Claim that former PM Oli had died of a heart attack (video of 23 September 2025)

properties.statement: A TikTok video posted on 23 September 2025 carried the text 'Heartfelt condolence. Former Prime Minister KP Oli is no more.'
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal states that Oli was alive. At the time he had been flown to an army barrack after resigning on 9 September and later moved to a rented apartment in Bhaktapur.

entities.title: Fabricated statement attributed to Army Chief Sigdel (March 2025)

properties.statement: A statement attributed to Army Chief Ashok Raj Sigdel said: 'Nepal Army has finally made its position clear. We are the soldiers of the nation but not the government. We are ready to abide by the people's decision.'
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal says the Army spokesperson confirmed the army did not issue it. A retired Indian Army major general shared a screenshot on X on 9 March 2025, the day thousands of pro-monarchy supporters welcomed former King Gyanendra Shah in Kathmandu. Build-up period.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: Video said to show Army Chief Sigdel saying the king should be placed at the centre

properties.statement: A video shared in 2026 carried the claim that Army Chief Ashok Raj Sigdel said the country was in a sensitive state and the king should be placed at the centre.
properties.verification_note: Result given: misleading. Newschecker Nepal says the video was an older clip posted in January 2026 and there is no evidence that Sigdel made the statement.

entities.title: Claim that Balen Shah was appointed prime minister or head of state in September 2025

properties.statement: In September 2025, TikTok and Facebook posts claimed Kathmandu mayor Balendra Shah had been appointed prime minister or head of state, one adding that activists had set fire to the prime minister's wife.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. Newschecker Nepal found the video recycled from an earlier oath ceremony; Fact Crescendo found Shah held no national post and that Sushila Karki became interim prime minister.

properties.statement: Indian television channels suggested that the businessman Durga Parsai (as spelled by Decode) played a central role in the protest.

entities.title: Photos of a man from Darjeeling presented as the architect of the Gen Z movement

properties.statement: Indian news channels News18 and Zee News published photos of a man from Darjeeling, claiming he was a key architect of the Gen Z movement, in a case of mistaken identity with the Hami Nepal coordinator.
properties.verification_note: Source is a Darjeeling-based journalist quoted by IPS. IPS says the case nearly painted the movement as India-sponsored. The man's name is not used here.

entities.title: Claim that the Gen Z protests were a demand for a Hindu state or monarchy

properties.statement: Posts and broadcasts in India described the September 2025 protests as a movement demanding a Hindu nation (Hindu Rashtra) or the restoration of the monarchy.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false or baseless. AFP says old footage of protesters calling for a Hindu monarchy was falsely shared as evidence. IPS, The Diplomat Nepal and The Quint reach the same finding. Related: claim:sikkim-rally-video-shown-as-nepali-protesters-for-hindu-rashtra-or-modi.

entities.title: Claim that protesters wanted Narendra Modi or Yogi Adityanath as their leader

properties.statement: Indian posts and channels claimed that Nepali protesters wanted a leader like Narendra Modi or Yogi Adityanath, or that they demanded Modi as their prime minister.
properties.verification_note: Assessment: false. The Quint says neither claim reflected reality on the ground; Decode (BOOM) reports that a student protester called the Modi claim 'utterly absurd and laughable'. The banner photo is covered by claim:yogi-adityanath-poster-photo-shown-as-from-nepal-gen-z-protests.

entities.title: AI-generated images and videos of Parliament and Singha Durbar burning circulated before the protests

properties.statement: AI-generated photos and videos of Parliament and Singha Durbar being burned or destroyed circulated on social media before the 8 September 2025 protests.
properties.verification_note: Kantipur, reporting the facts-and-analysis section of an official commission report (27 May 2026), and Onlinekhabar's one-year retrospective (8 September 2026) both state this. Onlinekhabar's October 2025 report on Cyabra says AI-generated images built momentum before the protest. Kantipur's retrievable text does not name the commission.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: Commission: protests were incited through AI, fake police pages and hacking

properties.statement: A commission report, as reported by Kantipur on 27 May 2026, says the protests were incited through AI-generated content, fake pages impersonating the police and hacking.
properties.verification_note: Only the headline and first paragraph of the Kantipur article could be retrieved. Details of the fake police pages and hacking are not available in the retrieved text, and the commission is not named there. Not independently confirmed.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: Cyabra: about one third of online discourse on the protests came from fake accounts

properties.statement: Cyabra, an Israel-based cyber intelligence firm, said in October 2025 that nearly 34 percent of online discourse during the 8 and 9 September protests was driven by fake accounts and AI-generated content.
properties.verification_note: The two Nepali reports describe the same Cyabra analysis differently. Onlinekhabar says 34 percent of the online discourse was driven by fake accounts and AI content. Republica says fake accounts made up 34 percent of sampled profiles on X, that they generated 11.5 percent of engagements (over 164,000 interactions), and that genuine users drove the bulk of protest activity. The underlying Cyabra report was not retrieved, and the analysis is of a sample on X.

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: Attendance figures for the Discord debate on an interim leader

properties.statement: More than 10,000 people joined the Youth Against Corruption Discord channel to debate an interim leader, and about 6,000 more watched a mirrored YouTube livestream.
properties.verification_note: Al Jazeera (15 September) gives more than 10,000 in the channel plus about 6,000 on YouTube. Decode (24 September) quotes one participant's recollection of about 30,000 to 35,000 people listening to the main call. The Kathmandu Post (29 September) counts 7,713 votes in the open poll and notes there is no official platform data to verify participation and that anonymity may have allowed repeat voting. These measure different things (channel members, listeners, votes). Timing of the debate is reported inconsistently across sources: Al Jazeera places it on Thursday (11 September).

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: Indian TV claim that the Gen Z protest was a CIA plot

properties.statement: Republic TV said on air that the Nepal protest was 'a pure CIA plot'.
properties.verification_note: Reported by Newslaundry (9 September 2025), which criticises the foreign-hand claims as an attempt to shift the story from Nepal's governance crisis to a geopolitical thriller. No source retrieved offers evidence for the claim.

properties.verification_note: Reported and criticised by Newslaundry (9 September 2025). No source retrieved supports the funding claim.

properties.verification_note: Reported and criticised by Newslaundry (9 September 2025), which says the foreign-hand framing sidelined domestic causes. No evidence for the claim was retrieved.

entities.title: Chinese social media users suspected a US and India role in the Nepal unrest

properties.statement: Chinese social media users suspected that the United States, and India, were behind the unrest in Nepal, and one cited a US $500 million Millennium Challenge Corporation grant.
properties.verification_note: StratNews Global (10 September 2025) records these as netizen opinions and adds no rebuttal or evidence.

entities.title: Oli and CPN-UML: the uprising was a foreign conspiracy or planned plot

properties.statement: KP Sharma Oli dismissed the deaths of young protesters as a foreign conspiracy and an attempt to burn the country, and CPN-UML described 8 and 9 September as a dangerous plan to push the country into authoritarianism, anarchy and geopolitical conflict.
properties.verification_note: Oli's words come from an Onlinekhabar opinion piece (7 March 2026), not a direct transcript. The UML statement (9 September 2026) names no group or country. No source retrieved provides evidence of foreign involvement.

evidence.note: Status describes how well the fact-check outcome is established across independent publishers.

entities.title: CPN-UML claim that infiltrators turned the peaceful protest violent

properties.statement: CPN-UML said that criminal groups infiltrated a peaceful youth protest on 9 September 2025 and turned it violent, using young protesters as human shields and encouraging the attack on Parliament.
properties.verification_note: CPN-UML's 2026 statement and an Onlinekhabar opinion piece (12 September 2025) support the infiltration account. The investigation commission, as reported by Onlinekhabar, said attacks on state structures cannot be confined to being merely impulsive, but it also found the use of guns and metal bullets was a mistake on the government's side. Balendra Shah, then Kathmandu mayor, said the 9 September incident was triggered by the government's excessive, terrorist-style use of force on 8 September.

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: Nepal Police: necessary force was ordered only after other forms of force were exhausted

properties.statement: Nepal Police said the 8 September 2025 order to use necessary force was given only after approval from the government security committee and after all other forms of force permitted under Nepali law had been exhausted.
properties.verification_note: The statement comes from Nepal Police as reported by BBC Eye Investigations (via Onlinekhabar, 26 February 2026). The same report cites a leaked police log in which 'Peter 1', identified by a source as former IGP Khapung, ordered 'use necessary force' ten minutes after the curfew began, and BBC video analysis of a minor who was unarmed and leaving the scene peacefully before he was killed. A human-rights activist told Onlinekhabar that police provoked protesters by firing tear gas and water cannon, and the investigation commission concluded the use of guns and metal bullets was a mistake on the government's side.

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: Government account: casualties occurred as the Special Task Force blocked entry to a vital installation

properties.statement: Those in power said the casualties on 8 September 2025 occurred when the Special Task Force of the Nepal Police tried to prevent protesters from entering a sensitive area or vital installation.
properties.verification_note: Onlinekhabar (8 September 2026) says Oli and other leaders, officials and security personnel repeated this before the inquiry commission and in court responses. Human-rights activists describe disproportionate and unusually lethal use of force, and the commission concluded that the use of guns and metal bullets was a mistake on the government's side.

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: Oli: he did not order police to open fire; the prime minister does not order police

properties.statement: In written statements to the Gauri Bahadur Karki-led inquiry panel and the National Human Rights Commission, Oli denied personal involvement in ordering police to open fire on the first day, and said the prime minister does not issue orders to the police.
properties.verification_note: The Kathmandu Post (5 January 2026) attributes the account to an official, not to a direct quote. Police told BBC Eye Investigations the force directive followed approval from the government security committee. The investigation commission recommended a criminal investigation against Oli, then Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak and then IGP Chandra Kuber Khapung, and said Oli's failure to prevent further loss of life was a major weakness. The commission did not, in the retrieved text, state that Oli gave a firing order.

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: CDO Rijal: he ordered rubber bullets below the knee, not final force

properties.statement: Kathmandu Chief District Officer Chhabilal Rijal told the probe commission he gave a verbal order to fire rubber bullets targeted below the knee but did not give the order of final force.
properties.verification_note: In the same statement Rijal said he heard on the police radio set that first the Inspector General of Police and then the acting chief of the Kathmandu Valley Police Office gave the order 'open fire as necessary to bring the situation under control'. BBC Eye Investigations (via Onlinekhabar) cites a police log with a 'use necessary force' order from 'Peter 1'. Both accounts name police commanders, not the CDO, as ordering lethal force; they are not independently confirmed.

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: Ministry of Health death toll of 36 (12 September 2025)

properties.statement: The Ministry of Health reported on 12 September 2025 that the death toll from the protests had reached 36, with 1,760 injured nationwide, based on hospital data.
properties.verification_note: Later counts are higher: 72 (Chief Secretary, 14 September) and 74 (Kathmandu police, 17 September). The 36 is a hospital-based count at one date, so it differs from later cumulative counts that include prisoners and security personnel.

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: Prison department figure of 13,591 escaped inmates and 964 children (19 September 2025)

properties.statement: The director of the Department of Prison Management, Chomendra Neupane, said on 19 September 2025 that 13,591 of 29,212 inmates and 964 of 1,422 children had escaped, with 8,816 still unaccounted for.
properties.verification_note: Police gave 14,507 inmates on 11 September. Neupane's figure is a later count by the prison authority.

evidence.note: Sources conflict; see verification_note.

entities.title: False reports of the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar spread in Indian media

properties.summary: Indian outlets, and The Business Standard citing family sources, reported on 9 September 2025 that Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar, wife of former Prime Minister Jhalanath Khanal, had died after protesters set their home on fire. Fact-checkers and Khanal himself said on 11 and 12 September that she was alive and in critical condition. See claim:chitrakar-died-on-9-september.

evidence.note: Reports of death (9 September) conflict with fact-checks and the husband's statement (11 to 12 September). The end date is the date of the last fact-check retrieved.

entities.title: Old Pashupatinath Temple footage spreads as an attack by protesters

properties.summary: From 9 September 2025 a video of a crowd at the gate of Pashupatinath Temple was shared and broadcast in India as protesters attacking the temple. AFP, Newschecker, BOOM and Alt News traced it to a festival procession in March 2025, and a monk told AFP that everything was peaceful inside the temple.

evidence.note: First post date 9 September comes from IPS; no end date is given because the sources do not state when the claim stopped circulating.

entities.title: AI-generated videos of Parliament burning circulate before the protest

properties.summary: Before the protest of 8 September 2025, pseudonymous accounts posted AI-generated images and videos showing Parliament and Singha Durbar burning, gunfire and tear gas. A commission report cited by Kantipur and Onlinekhabar's retrospective both describe this. Cyabra's analysis, as reported by Onlinekhabar, says AI-generated images built momentum before the real protest.

evidence.note: Sources say 'before the protests' without a date, so only the month is given.

entities.title: Indian TV channels broadcast foreign-hand theories about the protests

properties.summary: On or before 9 September 2025 Indian news channels linked the protests to a foreign hand: Republic TV called it a CIA plot, Times Now Navbharat spoke of a China-America struggle, and Aaj Tak said Hami Nepal had received Rs 20 crore from Coca-Cola and Viber. Newslaundry criticised the coverage in a piece of 9 September.

evidence.note: The date is Newslaundry's publication date; the broadcasts happened on or before it. Single source.

entities.title: Cyabra publishes analysis of fake accounts in Gen Z protest discourse

properties.description: Cyabra said 34 percent of sampled profiles on X in protest-related discourse were fake, that they generated 11.5 percent of engagements and had a potential reach of 326 million views. Reported by Republica and Onlinekhabar on 7 October 2025.

evidence.note: The date is that of the two Nepali reports; Cyabra's own publication date was not retrieved. The two reports describe the 34 percent figure differently, see claim:cyabra-one-third-of-protest-discourse-came-from-fake-accounts.

entities.title: Original Facebook post of the 'Malacañang slingshot' clip reported taken down

properties.description: VERA Files reported on 2 October 2025 that the original viral Facebook post of a Nepal Parliament protest video presented as a slingshot attack on Malacañang Palace, with more than 10 million views, had been taken down, while similar posts remained on other platforms. VERA Files does not say who removed it.

evidence.note: The date is the date of the VERA Files article; the removal date is not given.
